subject.title: fix(channels): honor configured read target policies

question: Should signed message-action context plus plugin-facing native-conversation and invocation-origin fields become the permanent host-to-plugin authorization contract?
rationale: The choice defines which runtime facts external plugins may trust before provider access and whether the resulting fail-closed compatibility change is intentional.

options.title: Compose And Adopt
options.body: Preserve the current identity-secret implementation, document the signed trust semantics, and require exact-head compatibility and live proof.

options.title: Keep Authority Internal
options.body: Enforce conversation policy through narrower host-owned adapters without adding plugin-facing trusted authorization inputs.

options.title: Split The Contract
options.body: Separate the runtime identity and public API changes from the individual channel policy gates before landing.

recommendation.title: Compose And Adopt
recommendation.body: Preserve the current identity-secret implementation, document the signed trust semantics, and require exact-head compatibility and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest merged-history ownership across the central routing, runtime, and plugin-loading boundaries involved in this decision.
